qualification: local A05.4 precise read, write, and generated atomic page-fault recovery acceptance; not hardware, cross-host, A05.3 dispatcher reduction, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.acceptedBoundary: A shared generated status decoder now publishes the resolver BLR continuation PC only for typed DORY_JIT_ATOMIC_RESOLUTION_PAGE_FAULT results from exchange, fetch-add, general binary RMW, unary RMW, bit-test RMW, and pair compare-exchange. Direct compare-exchange retains its separately accepted typed path.
candidate.failClosedBoundary: Successful atomic resolution continues in generated code. Fallback and error results return to the interpreter without a recovery PC or speculative recovery context.
candidate.recoveryContract: The instruction-entry checkpoint restores the exact faulting atomic instruction state, while the per-instruction side table publishes only the completed prefix and deoptimizes the faulting instruction to the interpreter. Read and terminator-safe write recovery retain their separately accepted paths.

verification.focused: 60 tests in the DBT ABI, metadata-fault, restartability, and PC Linux boot runner suites passed.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,553 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the same pinned inputs were executed explicitly twice.
verification.targetedCoverage: A real MAP_JIT matrix covers ordinary write, direct compare-exchange, exchange, fetch-add, locked add, locked increment, locked bit-test, and pair compare-exchange page faults. A cross-page atomic fallback regression proves that non-page-fault outcomes expose neither a recovery PC nor recovery context.

disposition.reason: The named restartability and latency matrix, exact metadata and checkpoint tests, fail-closed atomic status coverage, deterministic aggregate, and two independent clean production runs satisfy the A05.4 action and check without relaxing their bounds.

limitations: Two passing local runs are a bounded reliability check, not cross-host qualification.
The production fixture proves overall reliability but does not assert that every generated atomic helper faulted during the runs; the MAP_JIT matrix supplies that targeted proof.
This evidence does not satisfy the greater-than-95-percent A05.3 dispatcher gate or G1-G5.
